Episode 259. The Truth of the World, Your Truth, My Truth (12)
Jin and Murakan stared at Elona.

"...Lady Misha is right. It is not an eternal farewell. However, I do not know when Lord Jin will be able to meet Murakan and Lady Misha again, so I feel sorry. Whether it takes a year, ten years, or even longer... I do not know."
From the perspective of the beings called immortals and dragons, it wasn't a very long time. But by human standards, it was a distant future.
However, Murakan's face instantly brightened and he nodded his head.

[Who cares if it's a year or a hundred years. Ah, a hundred years won't do. They'll all be old and dead. Ten years is, well, fine! Isn't that right, kid? The world is being restored, so what's the big deal if we can't meet for that long? Damn it, I just cried for nothing and embarrassed myself!]
It was a sacrifice he had already accepted with the thought that they would never meet again.
[To Strawberry Pie... tell her to enjoy her life to the fullest and wait just a little. But if I don't come back for too long, and if by chance a better guy comes along, tell her to get married.]
[Oh, right. You're saying something right for a change. That's a better future for Strawberry Pie too. What on earth does that child see in a bum like this?]
[Hah? Well, right. What would you know? How would you know what love is? All you know is how to have a gloomy one-sided crush.]
Thwack!
In the end, Misha's fist flew. Murakan, while his jaw was repeatedly knocked aside, tried to counterattack a few times, but the more he did, the stronger the fist he was hit with.
[Ow, it hurts! It hurts! Hey, stop hitting me, I have to go now!]
[You'll get the rest later.]
They could meet again.
With hope, Jin and his comrades were not just sad as they had been a moment ago. Anytime, anywhere, in any form, as long as they could meet again.
Still, Jin and his comrades hugged Murakan and Misha as if they were people they would never see again. Misha furrowed her brow, saying it was a bit creepy, but she didn't seem to truly dislike it.
[Veradin.]
"Lady Elona..."

[I don't think it's important whether a life is long or short. At least, that's how it is for me. There are people who are unhappy even if they live out their natural lifespan, and there are people who receive salvation even if they live a fleeting life. I suffered as a monster for many years, but the short time I lived as a person... was filled with meaning after meeting the patriarch.]
"Then I am glad. If you think so, my lady."

[So even if I scatter into the world and lose this form, please don't be too sad. I, who have become the mountains and fields, the wind and the sea, the land and the sky, will always be there, remembering my time with the patriarch.]
A heavy rumbling sound was heard from the distance.
It was the sound of the world being destroyed. Giant lands were screaming and splitting apart, and the seas were boiling and drying up.
Soon, the aftermath would rush into Morganiel's territory.
[I don't want to spend my final moments in a disorderly fashion. I will begin now. Everyone, please close your eyes and wait quietly.]

The people closed their eyes, holding each other's hands. Jin held Murakan's hand, Murakan reflexively grabbed Misha's hand, then let go in fright and took Valeria's hand, Valeria took Dante's hand, Dante took Syris's hand, Syris took Enya's hand...
Thus, everyone was holding hands.
Veradin couldn't bring himself to close his eyes and looked at Elona. Elona gently held Veradin's face with both her hands.
She slowly closed his eyes and kissed his forehead.
[Be well, Veradin.]
"Be well, Lady Elona."

He wanted to open his eyes again. But he worried that it might make things harder for Elona. As he was contemplating, Veradin felt that Elona's palms, which had been covering his eyelids, were no longer there.
Opening his eyes again, Veradin was faced with a ball of sun energy. That sun energy, which he could cradle in both his hands, was Elona.

The rest was all darkness. It was so dark that even the people standing right next to him were visible only as outlines, but someone grabbed Veradin's hand. It was Enya. Veradin cradled the sun energy in his remaining hand as if holding it in his arms.
Murakan and Misha scattered into particles and disappeared into the sun energy. Jin's hand, which had been holding Murakan's, was empty for a moment, but Valeria took that hand again.
[Jin, show me Shuri.]
At Helluram's voice, Jin took Shuri out of the Red Jade without a second word.
[Mya!]
[When I placed the curse of immortality on you, I wanted to show you eternal darkness. A darkness where only a scenery like this would continue.]
[Myamya...]

[When the light disappears and all life turns to ash. I had hoped that someone would watch that scene. In truth, even I did not have the confidence to exist alone in the empty abyss. That's why I made you unable to die. So that when such a world came, I could live with you.]
Shuri recognized that some dark energy was leaving her. The curse of immortality was being lifted.
[In the language of people, it could be described as vicious and selfish.]
[Myananya...]
Shuri closed her eyes, feeling Helluram's final touch.
[Beasts are foolish and pitiful creatures. Why do you not flee my hand? Well... it's not something I can understand. Your new master is kind to you, unlike me, so live the rest of your life happily.]
Soon, Helluram too began to lose her form in the darkness.
She scattered in all directions like a black stream of water, then flowed into the sun energy. The more she did, the whiter the sun energy became.
It became a single ball of light. Like the light that had first existed in the world at the beginning of time, it was illuminating the darkness alone.
At that point, it was so bright that no one could open their eyes. The Origin Stone, which had maintained the form of a staff, was also crumbling into fine pieces and being absorbed into the light.
The people holding hands felt each other's bodies trembling. It felt as if time had stopped in the fear and anticipation of whether the world could truly return.
Then, familiar voices began to be heard. Voices they thought they would never hear again were ringing in their ears.
"Huh...? What? Am I not dead?"
"Daytona?"
"Brother Linpa!?"
They were the voices of those who had died fighting. In the unfamiliar scenery they saw as soon as they woke up, they thought they had come to the afterlife.
But a moment later, the will of the light was transmitted to their minds. They could tell that the broken world was rising again.
All over the world, the dead were returning like that.

At the same time, the numerous errors that were the multiverse were closing. Even if they couldn't see it, everyone could tell. The dimensions that had started from the atrocity of history manipulation were closing.
All the distortions that had continued for a thousand years were disappearing. They were finally finding their proper place.
Their minds grew distant.
As their senses blurred, the people lost consciousness, remembering only the fact that they were holding each other's hands.
July 30th, 1805. The Garden of Swords.
A magician in a black robe, like mourning clothes, entered the garden.
It was Veradin. Since the world had been restored, he had always worn only black clothes. As a sign that he was still a sinner, and in memory of the departed Elona.
"Lord Veradin, how about you stop wearing other clothes now? It feels so gloomy every time I see you..."
"That's right, Lord Veradin. To many people, Lord Veradin is perceived as a hero, not a bad guy. I don't think you need to say, 'I am a sinner,' every time."
It was Dante and Enya. They had come to the Garden of Swords to see Jin. But Jin was not there, so they were having tea with the other knights.
"There are people who look on me favorably, but there are still countless people who shudder at the name Zipple. Until not a single such person is left, our family will all wear only black clothes."
"You're the only Zipple left now, my lord."
"No, there's one more, isn't there?"
Octavia. Veradin had come here to meet his aunt, who was in the underground prison of the Garden of Swords.

"Ah, Octavia. That one is hard to understand too. Anyway, since the world returned safely thanks to her declaring her surrender herself at the end, I told her she could just stay in prison as long as she wanted and then come out... but it seems she still has no intention of coming out."
It was Mary.

In fact, Octavia was surprisingly supported by a considerable number of the public. It was because the final battle with the Demon Army and the process of the world's restoration had been mostly revealed to the public.
Except for the fact that only Jin was the one who had regressed 'with his memories intact', the public knew everything.

Jin had suggested revealing that content as well, but it had been thwarted by his comrades' opposition. His comrades had silenced Jin with the logic that it was a secret they wanted to keep to themselves.

"No matter what, I can't understand the people who support Aunt Octavia. Does doing one good thing at the end make your sins disappear? If that's the logic, then everyone is a decent person. My aunt is a bad person. She knows that herself, which is why she doesn't leave the prison. The same goes for me."
Mary shrugged and took out two new cups, filling them with tea.
"Go and drink with your aunt."
"I dare not refuse the kindness of the heavenly Runcandels..."
"You're funny. You'll get hit for that."
Veradin looked at Mary's fist, took the teacups, and headed for the underground prison.
Octavia's room, unlike the other prisoners', had its door open.
"You're here."
"Yes."
Octavia looked at the teacup Veradin had put down for a long time before taking it in her hand. A year ago, when the world was being restored, she had not held anyone's hand.
"Stop visiting me now. People will point fingers. You, unlike me, did not commit your sins of your own will, so it's not good for you to be associated with me."
"Still, we're family, how can I do that?"
At those words, Octavia let out a chuckle and recalled what the deceased Kelliark had said.

"Survive and live out your natural lifespan. It wouldn't be such a bad thing to be reborn as a shining being for once. Or it's fine to become a monster the likes of which the world has never seen again, like me. Still, you are my younger sibling, aren't you?"
"Pardon?"
"It's what Kelliark of the Demon Army said to me. Seeing you say we're still family reminds me of it."
Still a sibling, still family.
The two remaining Zipfels in the world perceived each other that way.
"Wouldn't it be a better atonement to go outside and contribute your knowledge to magic education or research? Like me."
"It's not that I haven't thought about it. But all the magic I learned was specialized only in killing and destroying people. It's not the kind of knowledge needed in this era."

Still, aunt, you could quickly make a great contribution to research on magic that saves people... Veradin was about to say that, but he looked at her hands and feet and shook his head. The body that Octavia had destroyed herself had not returned when the world was restored.
"Well, if that's the case, it can't be helped."
"I have decided on my life, to not leave this prison until I die. I can't become a shining being or a monster, but this is just my own conclusion for atonement."
"Still... your final choice, aunt, definitely had a shining point. If you hadn't made that choice, Lady Elona wouldn't have been able to restore the world so safely."
"That is why I have at least earned the qualification to atone like this. I am fine, so you should take off your mourning clothes, your shroud. Didn't Lady Elona ask your friend so earnestly?"
Veradin didn't answer and sipped his tea.

"I heard that Jin's patriarch succession ceremony is the day after tomorrow. At least when you attend, wear a white robe like in the old days. Only the Runcandels can wear black clothes at that event."
"Yes... I was planning to do so anyway. Because people shouldn't forget that I was a Zipple, that I still use that name."
"If you yourself don't forget, it will be fine even if everyone else forgets."
At those words, Veradin nodded his head.
It was definitely an underground prison, but a warm breeze was blowing between the two from somewhere. Veradin smiled as he caught the wind in his hand. It felt as if Elona had come.

"You're right. Strangely, a warm wind like this blows here too, aunt. Let's continue to live like this, without forgetting. Who we were, what we did, and how we will live while atoning in the future."
Octavia brought the teacup to her lips for the first time.
"...Let's do that."
